items.headline: Falcons stampede the Saints — five rushing TDs on Monday night
items.body: Atlanta made a statement in the Superdome. Bijan Robinson ripped off 145 yards and a pair of scores while bruising back Brian Robinson punched in three more, and the Falcons ran for five touchdowns in a 45-24 romp. New Orleans had no answer on the ground all night. Atlanta climbs back to .500 (2-2); the Saints slip to 1-3.
items.say: Did you catch Monday night? The Falcons ran all over the Saints — five rushing touchdowns, 45-24, with two different running backs named Robinson doing the damage. The NFC South is a mess this year. You riding with anybody this season?

items.headline: Worst-to-wow — the White Sox grab a 2-0 ALDS lead
items.body: Nobody circled the White Sox in spring, and here they are. After sweeping the Astros in the Wild Card round — Chicago's first postseason series win since the 2005 World Series — the youngest roster left in the AL has a 2-0 stranglehold on the favored Guardians. Japanese slugger Munetaka Murakami has been mashing, and the bats haven't cooled (73 runs over their last 11 games). One more win and they're in the ALCS.
items.say: The White Sox — the team that was historically bad a couple years ago — are one win from the ALCS. It's their first playoff series win since 2005. You gotta love a worst-to-first story. You got a team still alive, or just here for the October chaos?

items.headline: Rays put the Yankees on the brink — up 2-0 in the ALDS
items.body: Tampa Bay keeps shoving. A game after Drew Rasmussen flirted with a no-hitter, the Rays pounced on a sloppy, error-filled night from New York to win Game 2 and go up 2-0 in the series. Ben Rice launched two home runs for the Yankees, but it wasn't close to enough. Now the Bronx is sweating — New York heads home needing three straight just to survive.
items.say: The Rays have the Yankees down 2-0 in their playoff series — even two Ben Rice homers couldn't save New York. The small-payroll team bullying the big one never gets old. You following the baseball playoffs at all?

items.headline: Chourio walks it off — top-seeded Brewers go for the sweep tonight
items.body: Milwaukee is having a blast. Young star Jackson Chourio delivered a walk-off to beat the Padres in Game 2 and hand the NL's No. 1 seed a 2-0 series lead. Now it shifts to San Diego, where the Brewers can finish off a sweep tonight (Game 3 at Petco Park). The Padres have exactly one job left: win, or go home.
items.say: The Brewers' young stud hit a walk-off to go up 2-0 on the Padres, and they can sweep it tonight. Nothing beats a win-or-go-home game. You catching any October baseball, or just the highlights?

items.headline: Lights out under the lights — F1's Singapore night race this weekend
items.body: One of the coolest spectacles in sports is back: Formula 1 tears through the streets of Singapore under the lights this weekend (race Sunday), and it's the season's final Sprint weekend too. The downtown night race is brutal — heat, humidity, barriers inches away and zero room for error. George Russell won here a year ago; the fight at the front is still simmering.
items.say: F1's got its Singapore night race this weekend — cars flying through downtown streets in the dark, it looks unreal on TV. One of the best events on the whole calendar. You ever watch any Formula 1, or is it a total mystery to you?

items.headline: Ouch — Tom Cruise's 'Digger' is shaping up as a historic bomb
items.body: The big swing missed. 'Digger,' the Iñárritu oil-tycoon satire that turned Tom Cruise into a potbellied, comb-over villain, opened to a brutal ~$12-15M and rough reviews (41% on Rotten Tomatoes) — and it's tracking as one of the year's biggest money-losers for Warner Bros. Give Cruise credit for the wild gamble; it just didn't land with audiences.
items.say: That weird Tom Cruise movie where he's unrecognizable — 'Digger' — totally bombed, like one of the biggest flops of the year. You kind of have to respect him for trying something that strange, though. You a Cruise guy, or did the trailer lose you?

items.headline: Big riffs incoming — Greta Van Fleet drop 'Palace for the People' Friday
items.body: For the rock-and-roll crowd: Greta Van Fleet's new album 'Palace for the People' lands this Friday (Oct 9). The Grammy-winning young throwbacks — the ones who sound like they time-traveled from 1971 — have been teasing it with the soaring 'Saw You Stand,' and they cut the record with producer Mike Elizondo. Big, retro, arena-sized riffs; perfect windows-down music.
items.say: Greta Van Fleet — that young band that sounds exactly like Led Zeppelin — have a new album out Friday. If you grew up on classic rock, it really scratches the itch. You have a band you always come back to?

items.headline: Steampunk Western meets anime — Netflix drops the 'Bass X Machina' teaser
items.body: From Studio Mir (the animators behind 'The Legend of Korra' and 'Devil May Cry') comes a gritty, gorgeous steampunk-Western series, with Brian Tyree Henry voicing a gunslinging lawman loosely inspired by the real-life marshal Bass Reeves. The teaser is all train chases, dusty shootouts and towering machines. It saddles up on Netflix Nov 3.
items.say: There's a wild new Netflix cartoon coming — a steampunk Western with Brian Tyree Henry as a gunslinging lawman, from the folks who made Legend of Korra. The teaser looks incredible. You watch any of the grown-up animated stuff, or not your thing?

items.headline: A whole new Star Wars trilogy — Spider-Man's director takes the wheel
items.body: Big news for the galaxy far, far away: Jon Watts (the Tom Holland 'Spider-Man' movies) is lined up to direct the first film of a brand-new Star Wars trilogy — Episodes X, XI and XII — written by Simon Kinberg. Word is Daisy Ridley could return as Rey. It's early (Disney hasn't officially greenlit it), but the internet is already in full meltdown.
items.say: Apparently they're doing a whole new Star Wars trilogy — the Spider-Man director's attached and Rey might be back. Star Wars fans are losing it, as usual. You still keep up with Star Wars, or did you tap out somewhere along the way?
